'''''Nerine humilis''''', commonly known as '''dwarf nerine''',<ref name = PZA/> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[subfamily]] Amaryllidoideae of the [[family (botany)|family]] Amaryllidaceae, [[native species|native]] to the Cape of South Africa.<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/51244/i-Nerine-humilis-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder – ''Nerine humilis'' | accessdate = 13 April 2018}}</ref> Growing to {{convert| 40|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall, it is a variable ([[Polymorphism (biology)|polymorphic]]) [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]] with narrow leaves appearing at the same time as umbels of 1–12 slender, crenellated flowers in shades of pink, in autumn. It is a summer dormant deciduous species, meaning that the top growth disappears for a period during summer months.<ref name = PZA>{{cite web | url = http://pza.sanbi.org/nerine-humilis | title = ''Nerine humilis'' | publisher = SANBI PlantZAfrica.com | accessdate = 13 April 2018}}</ref> Plants can be found in large colonies in their native habitat, the [[Fynbos]] of the [[Cape Floristic Region]], appearing to respond well to the frequent fires in the area.<ref name = PBS/>

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''humilis'' means "dwarf" or "low-growing".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref> The plants are more likely to be dwarf in habit towards the western end of their range.

This plant has been given the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF/><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants – Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 67 
| publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 12 April 2018}}</ref> It does not tolerate being frozen, so requires some protection during the winter months. In cooler temperate zones it is best grown in a pot. Overcrowding of bulbs in a pot also improves flowering.<ref name = PBS>{{cite web | url = https://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/NerineSpeciesTwo
| title = Nerine Species Two | publisher = The Pacific Bulb Society | accessdate = 13 April 2018}}</ref>
